claimBoundary: This catalog is a navigation layer over the canonical scenario catalog. Capability lenses and decision questions describe what a bounded public-data replay can demonstrate; they do not add evidence, change ReplayPack claims, establish causal effects, represent client work, or prove real-world decisions, deployment, adoption, or impact.

lenses.description: Availability time, economic time, revisions, and later disclosures remain separate instead of being collapsed into hindsight.
lenses.label: Point-in-time integrity
lenses.question: What was actually knowable at the decision boundary?

lenses.description: Initial releases, revisions, arithmetic envelopes, and sampling limits stay visible; a heuristic range is never relabelled as a forecast or confidence interval.
lenses.label: Revision and range discipline
lenses.question: Does the conclusion survive vintage changes and an explicitly uncalibrated range?

lenses.description: Outcomes preserve breaches, inside-range results, reversals, and failed promotion instead of presenting only favorable cases.
lenses.label: Stress and uncertainty
lenses.question: Where does the predeclared boundary hold, breach, or remain unevaluable?

lenses.description: Cases cover bank funding, policy rates, cash balances, repo conditions, auctions, yield curves, credit, and market positioning with explicit claim limits.
lenses.label: Financial systems and markets
lenses.question: How do funding, rates, liquidity, market structure, and balance-sheet constraints interact?

lenses.description: Only the seven-engine bank replays carry simulated execution and allocation artifacts; those values remain research boundaries, not performance.
lenses.label: Allocation and execution
lenses.question: What survives non-zero cost, capacity, and constrained allocation?

lenses.description: Typed artifacts, input locks, deterministic archives, hashes, evidence classes, and negative claim boundaries make the workflow auditable.
lenses.label: Data systems and governance
lenses.question: Can another person trace the inputs, transformations, claims, and exclusions?

lenses.description: Labor, inflation, fiscal, monetary, trade, and facility data are treated as population-level or system-level signals, not individual outcomes or policy-effectiveness proof.
lenses.label: Policy and population signals
lenses.question: What can an aggregate official indicator support without becoming a causal policy claim?

lenses.description: Household-facing indicators support bounded behavioral hypotheses while preserving the gap between aggregate movement and individual intent.
lenses.label: Households and behavior
lenses.question: What do aggregate spending, saving, credit, and housing signals reveal—and what motives remain unobserved?

lenses.description: Housing starts, construction spending, house prices, and new-home sales expose spatially relevant evidence while stopping short of local regeneration or equity claims.
lenses.label: Housing, construction, and place
lenses.question: How do national housing and construction indicators change a place-based question without answering it?

lenses.description: Energy stocks, production, orders, trade, and producer or cross-border prices provide bounded operational signals without firm-level causal attribution.
lenses.label: Real-economy operations
lenses.question: How do production, inventory, trade, and price shocks move through an operating environment?

pathways.description: Follow four cases where later vintages, revised denominators, or paired source formats could otherwise leak hindsight into a historical conclusion.
pathways.title: Revision-safe research

pathways.description: Move from disclosure boundaries through rate and liquidity stress to the narrower set of cases that actually run execution and allocation engines.
pathways.title: Funding, liquidity, and allocation

pathways.description: Compare monetary, fiscal, labor, and facility evidence while keeping policy context distinct from policy-effectiveness claims.
pathways.title: Policy signals without causal overreach

pathways.description: Read saving, spending, credit, construction, prices, starts, and sales together without converting national aggregates into individual motives or local outcomes.
pathways.title: Households, housing, and place

pathways.description: Trace inventories, production, orders, trade, and prices as separate official signals rather than compressing them into one retrospective story.
pathways.title: Real-economy shock chain

Reported changes remain reported; the -290-to--110-basis-point persistence-or-one-known-decline envelope remains inferred with no probability. The March event stays only in a disjoint event lock. This is not a BLS forecast, confidence interval, calibrated range, export-quantity or nominal-value measure, tariff, PPI, firm result, profit-and-loss, causal model, deployment, external validation, investment result, or user-impact claim.

claims.boundary: Artifact presence proves integration structure, not economic correctness.
limitations: External reproduction and domain review remain separate gates.
claims.statement: The pack contains outputs from the four engines relevant to this case.

claims.boundary: The two endpoints carry no probability or coverage claim.
limitations: The March event did not set or widen the range.
claims.statement: The next-release stress endpoints are February persistence or one repeat of the known 180-basis-point decline, from -290 to -110 basis points.

claims.boundary: This is internal fail-closed evidence, not external method validation.
limitations: No predictive or causal validity is inferred.
claims.statement: TrialCourt rejected the retrospective one-decline export-price attempt.

claims.boundary: These are aggregate export-price release facts, not shipment records.
limitations: The index is not quantity, nominal export value, tariff, PPI, or firm P&L.
claims.statement: The February 14 and March 13 BLS releases first reported all-export monthly changes of 0.7 and -1.1 percent.

claims.boundary: The sentinels are not orders, capital, capacity, or returns.
limitations: They exist only to exercise mandatory adversarial checks.
claims.statement: Trial operational values are simulated schema sentinels only.

scenarios.decisionQuestion: Can an inside-range export-price result remain an evaluation outcome rather than a success or firm-performance claim?
